examples.text: Land Rover LR3 with 135k miles Tinted windows, AC works great, navigation. Exhaust modified by shop to be a little louder - V8 sounds fantastic. The interior is almost perfect, the side of driver seat starting to wear but everything else is in amazing condition. Previous owner had the transmission filter changed and had a full power flush done which makes sure ALL transmission fluid gets changed out. Good tires, good all time AWD. The extra 4wd modes work great. Stereo is fantastic. Passes emissions flawlessly. I converted the suspension from the default LR air suspension to traditional coil suspension and since then it has been nothing but smooth. I had the belt, coolant pump replaced when we converted the suspension, plus we have also gotten a new battery since getting the car. The electric parking brake doesn't work. It has been this way since I've owned it. This is very common with these cars and I have not had it looked at for repair at all because... well we live in Tucson and its flat... This vehicle is amazing to drive. The 3rd row has lots of legroom. Center console has a small built in "cooler" you can put drinks in. OEM rubber mats in the front and back seats. There is an aftermarket floor mat in the cargo area. There are a few scratches but it is in good condition for its age. The other similar LR3 for sale currently in AZ is listed for price_removed ! examples.text: 2002 Audi A4, 3.0 V6 Auto Has around 180k miles. I bought the car around 4 years ago and it has always been great for me. Multiple trips up and down the east and west coast and a fully packed drive across the country and it has never let me down once, just kept up on normal maintenance; oil changes, brakes, tires, control arms, etc. with that being said it does have some issues. The bad: Currently needs to be jumped in order to start. It has a newer battery replaced sometime in fall 2020, but it needs an alternator. Electrical- the wipers act up, the radio doesn’t work but seems to always be drawing power, alarm and lock/unlock horns don’t work, some other little things I’m probably forgetting. Pretty sure this can all be traced back to the alternator issue. Exhaust- pretty rotted out. Has holes, is held up with cables in spots. Check engine light is on for the catalytic converters as well. Squeeking noise from front right whenever turning or going over bumps. The good: Almost new 225/40-18 run flat blizzaks on Vw gti wheels. Tires alone cost almost price_removed k and only have a couple hundred miles on them. Only drove this car during storm days since I bought a newer Audi. It’s been sitting for a month or so, really just don’t need it anymore. Fix it up and it’s a good car, or part it out and make some money. I can send more pics and info through text. examples.text: 1997 Aston Martin DB7 Volante. Designed by Ian Callum this flat out gorgeous hand built grand tourer which thoroughly embodies British royalty is finished in spectacular Black over Ivory Connolly leather interior and is complimented with black piping and burled walnut wood trimming and black Wilton carpeting. Factory equipment includes: :Power folding top which is stowed beneath a black boot in the rear :Power adjustable driver and passenger seats :Heated driver and passenger seats :Power windows and door locks :Cruise control :A/C with dual zone climate control :Alpine AM/FM cassette player with remote cd player and trunk mounted Alpine amplifier :Tilt Leather wrapped steering wheel :Unique 12 spoke aluminum wheels shod with brand new Goodyear F1 performance tires. Pampered and thoroughly serviced throughout it's life, this Aston is in outstanding and original condition both cosmetically and mechanically. There was a pre sale inspection performed in 2020 by the previous owner prior to the sale. It comes with 53 pages of service records from purchase in 1997 up through 2020 including all factory manuals, manufacturers literature, correspondence, trickle charger, storage bag, boot cover, all factory tools, Aston Martin detailing kit, 3-keys and 2 operational key fobs are included. Carfax report indicates an accident free history but in 2000 a not actual mileage title was issued to the previous owner as there was a replacement gauge cluster that was installed at 5,636 miles, this was a warranty issue. The six-digit odometer shows just under 35k miles, though the actual total is estimated to be approximately 40k. There is documentation showing the mileage and the date on which it was replaced. Also, An ABS sensor was repaired during the most recent service, though the former owner notes that the ABS warning light has illuminated intermittently throughout the cars life even though nothing wrong has been detected with the system itself. We have concluded that it’s down to an oversensitive fault detection system. The brakes always work fine and the light routinely goes out after driving it for a while. The drive train runs perfectly, and services have been done by dealer specialists since it was purchased in 2018. The Rapide has four doors and a hatchback, which makes it the “practical” Aston Martin, but it is also a very beautiful car, and a bit rare too with less than 2000 being made in 2010. Think of it as a supermodel who can wash dishes. The Rapide has been driven about 2,000 miles a year which included many longer drives from New Haven, CT to southern NJ and back. In the winter Miller Motor Cars in Stamford, CT performs the annual maintenance and repairs, she's then stored in the owner's garage under a car cover with a trickle charger until spring. It is a very sweet ride which gets a lot of positive attention. Many strangers pull up beside the Rapide, smile and give a “thumbs up.” It is a very cool car, but it is time for she and the owner to take different roads. The car was originally sold in NY and then made her way to the mid-west and deep south for a bit before coming back north to CT. The local Aston Martin dealership, Miller Motor Cars, administers the premium extended warranty and performed the bulk of the maintenance and repairs. The Carfax describes minor to moderate damage to the left side in 2017, but Autocheck gave this Rapide a score of 94 when she was purchased by the current (the 5th) owner in 2018 and has no mention of the damage. There is no evidence of work done, and in 2017, anything extensive would have totaled this car pretty easily, it is possible the Carfax is incorrect. The car has 29,970 miles and as an Aston Martin comes standard with many "high end" features, including tilt-telescoping steering wheel, 8 way, power, heated and cooled seats, bi-xenon headlamps and LED tail lamps. Leather and wood trim with aluminum accents; power front seats with memory; Bang & Olufsen 16-speaker sound system with two tweeters that rise from the dashboard on activation of the system; satellite radio with USB and iPod connectivity, Bonded aluminum chassis, 20-inch alloy wheels, Adjustable suspension, Front and rear parking sensors, Automatic climate control, Leather upholstery and alcantara head liner, Navigation system The car is painted in Canna Di Fucile (Gunmetal Grey metallic) over a Bitter Chocolate leather interior, which includes 4 bucket seats set down deep in the chassis. The 6 litre V12 is a DOHC, all aluminum (block and heads), 48 valve, monster that is super smooth in it's application of 510 HP and 420 lb-ft to the ground via the paddle shifted, 6 speed auto... growling as it moves up through the RPMs. The hatch back is decorated in matching alcantara suede to look like a set of fit luggage when closed. Both front and rear doors open in a "swan mode", out and up. There are a couple of foibles in this supermodel's fame. One very small ding on the left rear door, lines forming in the veneer on the nav system, very minor wear on the driver lower bolster, a small scuff under the front air dam and she's missing the under engine tray. The Carfax shows regular maintenance throughout her life and the current owner has a file of every receipt since his ownership which includes: Replaced driver’s side front fender liner, Performed TCU re-flash per Aston Martin campaign RA-07-0028, Replaced front tie-rod assemblies, Performed 4-wheel tire alignment, Replaced windshield washer motors, Replaced rear brake pads and sensors, Replaced front left marker light, Replaced front brake pads, Performed Annual Service (two-year) including oil change and filter replacement, Performed differential servicing, Performed coolant flush, Replaced engine drive belt, Performed annual one-year service including oil change Replaced front left headlight assembly, Replaced battery and performed minor paint touch-up on front bumper and wheels, Replaced tires with new Bridgestone Potenza S001 tires (in 2018, 245/40 ZR20 in F, 295/35 ZR 20 R), all within the last 6000 miles. The car has two crystal keys and one emergency metal key, along with a custom fit car cover and trickle charger that come with the car. If ever there was a true Sport Saloon, this is it! It will accelerate 0 to 60 MPH in 4.7 seconds. Sold originally in 2010 for roughly price_removed this car can now be had in nearly new condition, with very low mileage for almost a quarter of that original asking price. price_removed will take her to a new home. Any questions, for many more photos and video, to schedule a time to see her in person, or to make an offer, please don't hesitate to contact me. Thank you for the interest.

examples.text: Campagnola Own a piece of history with this 1980 Fiat Campagnola, imported from Italy to the US two years ago. Less than two dozen are known to exist in the US, with this likely being the only soft top that was imported. The vehicle is a tank with similar models used extensively in European militaries, as well as a Pope-Mobile. The SUV is finished in beige with black vinyl seats, the truck features selectable four-wheel drive, a removable soft top, and bench seating in the cargo area. Power is from a 2.0-liter inline-four paired with a five-speed manual transmission and a dual-range transfer case. The exterior was repainted in beige and an unknown point and features a folding windshield, removable upper doors with sliding windows, and a black frame for its canvas soft top. Carello headlamps with city and spot lights are mounted at the front, while European-market rear lighting includes a fog light on the left and a reverse lamp on the right. The cab features seats trimmed in black vinyl, a T-shaped aluminum handle on the center console for engaging four-wheel drive, and a shifter for the high-low transfer case mounted beside the driver’s seat. The rear cargo area features sideways troop-style seating on wood platforms over the wheel wells. The truck is equipped with four-wheel independent torsion bar suspension, six interchangeable shock absorbers, and adjustable ride height and was considered to be superior to the Land Rover and Land Cruiser during it’s time. Recent maintenance is said to have included replacement of the brake pads, engine oil, transmission fluid, differential fluid, new clutch cable, and new belts. SUV has a clean Pennsylvania title. Instrumentation includes a 140-kph speedometer and gauges for water temperature and fuel level. The five-digit odometer shows just under 22k kilometers (~14k miles), with actual mileage unknown. Vehicle runs great, and can comfortably cruise at 60-65mpg on the highway, while still being able to climb hills like a mountain goat. It can climb a 50 degree hill as well as traverse a 40 degree side slope. Extra parts include a spare rim which hasn’t been mounted, extra belts, as well as cylinder head gaskets. #SUV #LandCruiser #Land Cruiser #LandRover #Land Rover #4runner #pinzgauer #unimog #Toyota #Jeep #FJ Cruiser #4x4 #Lexus #Overland
